claim: The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria is asymmetric, with the inner leaflet composed of glycerophospholipids (GPLs) and the outer leaflet predominantly composed of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or lipooligosaccharide (LOS).
source: While the inner leaflet of the OM is composed of the standard glycerophospholipids (GPLs), the outer leaflet is predominantly lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or lipooligosaccharide (LOS) (Funahara and Nikaido, 1980; Schindler and Osborn, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Funahara and Nikaido, 1980; Schindler and Osborn, 1979).

claim: LPS and LOS differ by the presence or absence of O-antigen sugar repeats respectively.
source: LPS or LOS differ by the presence or absence of O-antigen sugar repeats respectively, but both molecules are anchored in the OM by lipid A, a unique glycolipid, that is remarkably conserved amongst Gram-negative bacteria (Whitfield and Trent, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Whitfield and Trent, 2014).

claim: Lipid A is a bis-phosphorylated glucosamine disaccharide that can be anywhere from tetra- to hepta-acylated depending on genera.
source: Lipid A is a bis-phosphorylated glucosamine disaccharide that can be anywhere from tetra- to hepta-acylated depending on genera (Whitfield and Trent, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Whitfield and Trent, 2014).

claim: The increased hydrophobicity of lipid A strongly excludes the passive entry of hydrophilic compounds.
source: This increased hydrophobicity is the first reason for the OM's functionality as a barrier, as it strongly excludes the passive entry of hydrophilic compounds (Nikaido, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Nikaido, 2003).

claim: Negatively charged phosphates on lipid A and covalently attached sugars increase the net negative charge of the outer membrane, facilitating efficient cross-bridging with divalent cations.
source: Secondly, negatively charged phosphates on lipid A and covalently attached sugars that make up the core of LPS/LOS increases the net negative charge of the outer membrane. This facilitates efficient cross-bridging with divalent cations in the environment and promotes strong lateral interactions between LPS/LOS molecules on the surface (Schindler and Osborn, 1979; Murata et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Schindler and Osborn, 1979; Murata et al., 2007).

claim: Tightly packed LPS/LOS molecules serve as physical impediments to the accessibility of hydrophobic compounds to the lipid bilayer of the OM.
source: These tightly packed LPS/LOS molecules, particularly the core and O-antigen sugars, serve as physical impediments to the accessibility of hydrophobic compounds to the lipid bilayer of the OM (Funahara and Nikaido, 1980; Schindler and Osborn, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Funahara and Nikaido, 1980; Schindler and Osborn, 1979).

claim: A large majority of antibiotic classes are ineffective on Gram-negative bacteria due to either the inability to diffuse across the membrane or rapid efflux out of the cytoplasmic space.
source: A large majority of antibiotic classes are ineffective on Gram-negative bacteria due to either the inability to diffuse across the membrane (Nikaido, 1994; Vergalli et al., 2020) or rapid efflux out of the cytoplasmic space (Du et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Nikaido, 1994; Vergalli et al., 2020; Du et al., 2018).

claim: The Lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) pathway forms a transmembrane bridge to transport LPS/LOS to the OM.
source: The Lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) pathway forms a transmembrane bridge to transport LPS/LOS to the OM (Okuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Okuda et al., 2016).

claim: The Localization of lipoprotein (Lol) system transports lipoproteins from the IM to the OM.
source: The Localization of lipoprotein (Lol) system transports lipoproteins from the IM to the OM (Grabowicz, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Grabowicz, 2019).

claim: The β-barrel assembly machinery (Bam) facilitates folding and insertion of outer membrane proteins (OMPs).
source: The β-barrel assembly machinery (Bam) facilitates folding and insertion of outer membrane proteins (OMPs) (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2011).

claim: Bacterial cells can rapidly and efficiently transport GPLs in the retrograde direction (OM to IM).
source: Additionally, previous work done by Mary Jane Osborn's group highlighted the ability for bacterial cells to rapidly and efficiently transport GPLs in the retrograde direction (OM to IM) (Jones and Osborn, 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Jones and Osborn, 1977).

claim: Deletion of the Tol-Pal system negatively impacts bulk retrograde GPL transport.
source: There is evidence that deletion of the Tol-Pal system negatively impacts bulk retrograde GPL transport, although whether this is direct or indirectly mediated by Tol-Pal remains to be determined (Shrivastava et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Shrivastava et al., 2017).

claim: Mutants of E. coli lacking the Mla pathway were susceptible to combinatorial exposure to SDS/EDTA.
source: The Mla pathway was discovered in 2009, where it was found that mutants of E. coli lacking this pathway were susceptible to combinatorial exposure to SDS/EDTA (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).

claim: Susceptibility to detergent + chelator combinations indicate perturbed OM asymmetry.
source: Susceptibility to detergent + chelator combinations indicate perturbed OM asymmetry, as E. coli is typically highly resistant due to the lateral LPS interactions (Schindler and Osborn, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Schindler and Osborn, 1979).

claim: Spontaneous suppressors that could alleviate sensitivity to SDS/EDTA in Mla mutants all achieved increased expression of pldA.
source: Spontaneous suppressors that could alleviate sensitivity all achieved the same result – increased expression of pldA (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).

claim: PldA has an active site that is exclusively exposed to the outer leaflet of the OM.
source: PldA is an outer membrane phospholipase which, demonstrated through extensive crystallographic and biochemical analyses, has an active site that is exclusively exposed to the outer leaflet of the OM (Brok et al., 1996; Scandella and Kornberg, 1971; Snijder et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Brok et al., 1996; Scandella and Kornberg, 1971; Snijder et al., 1999).

claim: PldA enzymatically degrades GPLs that are mislocalized to the outer leaflet of the OM.
source: As such, PldA enzymatically degrades GPLs that are mislocalized to the outer leaflet of the OM.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the known function and localization of PldA.

claim: Mla and PldA have overlapping functionalities albeit through distinct mechanisms.
source: Through this suppression analysis, it was reasonably hypothesized that Mla and PldA have overlapping functionalities albeit through distinct mechanisms (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).

claim: The Mla system is comprised of 6 proteins: MlaA, MlaC, MlaD, MlaE, MlaF, and MlaB.
source: The intact, functional system is comprised of 6 proteins (Powers and Trent, 2019). MlaA is an alpha-helical outer membrane lipoprotein (Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017). MlaC is a soluble, periplasmic protein (Huang et al., 2016). MlaD is anchored in the inner membrane with a lipid-binding MCE domain in the periplasmic space (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016). It is coupled in a tight complex with an inner membrane permease, MlaE, a cytoplasmic ATPase, MlaF, and a cytoplasmic accessory protein MlaB (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2019; Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2016; Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).

claim: MlaA is an alpha-helical outer membrane lipoprotein.
source: MlaA is an alpha-helical outer membrane lipoprotein (Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017).

claim: MlaC is a soluble, periplasmic protein.
source: MlaC is a soluble, periplasmic protein (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Huang et al., 2016).

claim: MlaD is anchored in the inner membrane with a lipid-binding MCE domain in the periplasmic space.
source: MlaD is anchored in the inner membrane with a lipid-binding MCE domain in the periplasmic space (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).

claim: MlaD is coupled in a tight complex with an inner membrane permease MlaE, a cytoplasmic ATPase MlaF, and a cytoplasmic accessory protein MlaB.
source: It is coupled in a tight complex with an inner membrane permease, MlaE, a cytoplasmic ATPase, MlaF, and a cytoplasmic accessory protein MlaB (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Ekiert et al., 2017; Thong et al., 2016).

claim: Structural analyses and genetic data support the hypothesis that the Mla pathway functions in a retrograde manner.
source: Structural analyses and subsequent genetic data further bolstered the hypothesis that the Mla pathway functions in the initially proposed retrograde manner (Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017; Baarda et al., 2019; Chong et al., 2015; Sutterlin et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Abellón-Ruiz et al., 2017; Baarda et al., 2019; Chong et al., 2015; Sutterlin et al., 2016).

claim: A. baumannii can survive in the absence of LOS.
source: A. baumannii is relatively unique in that it can survive in the absence of LOS, which is typically essential in Gram-negative organisms (Powers and Trent, 2018b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2018b).

claim: In the absence of LOS, the lipid composition of A. baumannii OM is exclusively a symmetric GPL bilayer.
source: In this case, the lipid composition of its OM is exclusively a symmetric GPL bilayer (Powers and Trent, 2018a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2018a).

claim: LOS-deficient populations of A. baumannii rapidly inactivated genes in the Mla pathway and occasionally pldA.
source: What we found overwhelmingly was that when given the opportunity, LOS-deficient populations across multiple strains of A. baumannii rapidly inactivated genes in the Mla pathway and occasionally pldA (Powers and Trent, 2018a), a finding that was independently corroborated by the Kahne group (Nagy et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2018a; Nagy et al., 2019).

claim: The UW ΔmlaF mutant exhibits a significant growth defect compared to its isogenic parent.
source: While the UGA ΔmlaF mutant grows identically to its isogenic parent (red and black triangles, respectively), the UW ΔmlaF strain exhibited a significant growth defect (green and orange circles, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The increases in optical density during exponential phase of the UW ΔmlaF strain were due to growth.
source: Quantification by colony forming units from hours 1 to 4 confirmed that, despite its unexpected growth defect, increases in optical density during exponential phase were due to growth (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain appeared morphologically distinct in both size and color from its parent when grown on agar plates.
source: Furthermore, the UW ΔmlaF strain appeared morphologically distinct in both size and color from its parent when grown on agar plates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by visual evidence shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: No published mla mutants exhibit any growth defects across genera.
source: This growth defect was surprising as as no mla mutants in A. baumannii (Powers and Trent, 2018a), Burkholderia cepacia (Bernier et al., 2018), Neisseria gonorrhoeae (Baarda et al., 2019), Haemophilus influenzae (Fernández-Calvet et al., 2018), or E. coli (Ekiert et al., 2017; Chong et al., 2015) have been shown to have any growth defect compared to the isogenic parent.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2018a; Bernier et al., 2018; Baarda et al., 2019; Fernández-Calvet et al., 2018; Ekiert et al., 2017; Chong et al., 2015).

claim: Mutations that perturb OM homeostasis can alter the rate of vesiculation.
source: While this occurs naturally to varying extents across bacterial genera, mutations that perturb OM homeostasis can alter the rate of vesiculation.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about OM vesiculation.

claim: Both the UGA and UW ΔmlaF mutants exhibited ~2–4X increase in OMVs during exponential phase.
source: During exponential phase, both the UGA and UW ΔmlaF mutants exhibited ~2–4X increase in OMVs (Figure 1C), consistent with published data in other organisms (Roier et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and a citation to published literature (Roier et al., 2016).

claim: The UW ΔmlaF mutant had a 23X increase in OMV levels in stationary phase.
source: Strikingly, when we assessed stationary phase cultures for OMVs, there was a major discrepancy in the relative degrees of vesiculation between mutant and WT. Whereas the UGA ΔmlaF mutant maintained fold-changes relative to WT within the expected range, the UW ΔmlaF mutant had a staggering 23X increase in OMV levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain has a unique stationary phase lysis phenotype.
source: These data suggest that the UW ΔmlaF strain has a unique stationary phase lysis phenotype which has not been observed in other mla mutants.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the OMV data showing a 23X increase in stationary phase.

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF strain has a 3.2-fold increase in sensitivity to novobiocin compared to WT.
source: When we examined the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) for novobiocin, there was a 3.2-fold increase in sensitivity in the UGA ΔmlaF strain compared to a 5.85-fold increase in sensitivity of the UW ΔmlaF strain (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain has a 5.85-fold increase in sensitivity to novobiocin compared to WT.
source: When we examined the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) for novobiocin, there was a 3.2-fold increase in sensitivity in the UGA ΔmlaF strain compared to a 5.85-fold increase in sensitivity of the UW ΔmlaF strain (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF strain has a 1.8-fold increase in sensitivity to rifampicin compared to WT.
source: This trend of exacerbated sensitivity in the UW ΔmlaF were also seen with rifampicin, with 1.8-fold and 14-fold increases in sensitivity of the UGA and UW ΔmlaF respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain has a 14-fold increase in sensitivity to rifampicin compared to WT.
source: This trend of exacerbated sensitivity in the UW ΔmlaF were also seen with rifampicin, with 1.8-fold and 14-fold increases in sensitivity of the UGA and UW ΔmlaF respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF mutant exhibited no change in MIC for vancomycin.
source: The vancomycin results were particularly distinct. The UGA ΔmlaF mutant exhibited no change in MIC, while the UW ΔmlaF has a 2.3-fold increase in sensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain has a 2.3-fold increase in sensitivity to vancomycin compared to WT.
source: The vancomycin results were particularly distinct. The UGA ΔmlaF mutant exhibited no change in MIC, while the UW ΔmlaF has a 2.3-fold increase in sensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Kamischke et al. reported a ~50% decrease in GPL content in the OM of Δmla mutants.
source: The critical finding in Kamischke et. al. was a rather significant ~50% decrease in GPL content in the OM of Δmla mutants (Kamischke et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Kamischke et al., 2019).

claim: Attempts to achieve membrane separations in A. baumannii were unsuccessful using the Osborn protocol.
source: Despite an exhaustive approach, attempts in our laboratory to achieve membrane separations in A. baumannii were met with no success (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The gradient utilized by Kamischke et al. was insufficient to separate A. baumannii membranes.
source: Independently, a recent methods paper published during the review of this work demonstrated that the gradient utilized by Kamischke et al. was insufficient to separate A. baumannii membranes, further validating our results presented here (Cian et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Cian et al., 2020).

claim: All OMVs contain GPLs that have undergone anterograde transport from the IM to OM.
source: To do this, we relied on OM vesiculation as a proxy for anterograde transport, as all OMVs contain GPLs that have undergone anterograde transport from the IM to OM.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about OMV composition and biogenesis.

claim: Every Δmla mutant tested exhibited a significant increase in 32P-labeled lipids in the supernatant.
source: Instead, we observed a significant increase in 32P-labeled lipids in the supernatant in every Δmla mutant tested (Figure 2B & C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B & C.

claim: Both the UGA ΔmlaF and UW ΔmlaF mutant had increased 32P-labeled lipids in the OMV pulse-chase assay.
source: Both the UGA ΔmlaF and UW ΔmlaF mutant had increased 32P-labeled lipids using this assay, indicating no defect in anterograde transport (Figure 2B & C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B & C.

claim: UW mlaC::kan MJP1 and MJP2 mutants showed no defects in anterograde transport.
source: To remove strain differences as a variable, we constructed deletions of ΔmlaC in the UW WT background (UW mlaC::kan MJP1 and MJP2). Consistent with previous results, we saw no defects in anterograde transport as evidenced by an increase in 32P-labeled OMVs (Figure 2B & C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B & C.

claim: OMVs collected from the pulse-chase assay are enriched in OmpA compared to total membranes.
source: When blotted for OmpA, we observed OmpA enrichment in the OMV samples relative to total membranes which served as our control. This is consistent with the fact that OMVs are exclusively OM material (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: OMVs collected from the pulse-chase assay contain no IM protein as evidenced by lack of NADH oxidase activity.
source: In contrast, when assessed for NADH oxidase activity, only total membranes were enzymatically active, confirming that OMVs contained no IM protein (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain had a significantly different transcriptomic profile compared to its isogenic parent.
source: It was evident by principal components analysis (PCA) that the UW ΔmlaF strain had a significantly different transcriptomic profile compared to its isogenic parent (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF mutant clustered much closer to its isogenic parent by PCA.
source: In contrast, the UGA ΔmlaF mutant clustered much closer to its isogenic parent, consistent with results in another strain of A. baumannii published previously (Powers and Trent, 2018a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to published literature (Powers and Trent, 2018a).

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF and WT had 13 genes that were differentially expressed excluding mlaF.
source: While the UGA ΔmlaF and WT had 13 genes that were differentially expressed excluding mlaF (Supplementary file 1), the UW ΔmlaF and WT differed by 103 genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF and WT differed by 103 genes.
source: While the UGA ΔmlaF and WT had 13 genes that were differentially expressed excluding mlaF (Supplementary file 1), the UW ΔmlaF and WT differed by 103 genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 2.

claim: None of the 103 differentially regulated genes in the UW ΔmlaF were conserved in the UGA ΔmlaF.
source: When we looked at this array of 103 differentially regulated genes in the UGA ΔmlaF and WT, it was readily apparent that none of these changes were conserved between ΔmlaF mutants (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Genes involved in Csu pilus formation were significantly upregulated in the UW ΔmlaF.
source: The first cluster are genes involved in Csu pilus formation, which were significantly upregulated in the UW ΔmlaF (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The csu operon was downregulated in the UGA ΔmlaF relative to WT.
source: In fact, the csu operon was downregulated in the UGA ΔmlaF relative to WT (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Kamischke et al. reports an increase in biofilm formation in Δmla mutants.
source: Importantly, Kamischke et al. reports an increase in biofilm formation in Δmla mutants in their study: this transcriptional data confirms that the UW ΔmlaF provided to us is behaving similarly in our hands (Kamischke et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Kamischke et al., 2019).

claim: A large array of 70S ribosomal proteins were differentially regulated between the ΔmlaF mutants.
source: Interestingly, we found a large array of 70S ribosomal proteins were differentially regulated between the ΔmlaF mutants (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Additional genes involved in ribosome stability, transcription, and translation were differentially regulated between the ΔmlaF mutants.
source: Additional genes involved in ribosome stability, transcription, and translation were differentially regulated (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: One non-synonymous mutation in the coding region of the essential gene obgE was identified in the UW strains.
source: From this comparison, we were able to identify one non-synonymous mutation in the coding region of the essential gene obgE.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-genome sequencing.

claim: The obgE SNP in the UW WT and ΔmlaF resulted in a single amino acid change from an asparagine (N) to an isoleucine (I) at position 258 (N258I).
source: The obgE SNP in the UW WT and ΔmlaF resulted in a single amino acid change from an asparagine (N) to an isoleucine (I) at position 258 (N258I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-genome sequencing.

claim: The N258 position in obgE is highly conserved in A. baumannii.
source: Comparison of sequences of obgE from 14 published genomes affirmed that the N258 position is highly conserved in A. baumannii (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The nucleotide profile of the UW ΔmlaF with obgE* was strikingly different from all other strains tested.
source: What was immediately apparent was that the nucleotide profile of the UW ΔmlaF with obgE* was strikingly different from all other strains tested (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF was almost completely depleted of pppGpp, with a −12% shift when compared to WT.
source: The UW ΔmlaF was almost completely depleted of pppGpp, with a −12% shift when compared to WT (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF had +3% and +9% shifts in ppGpp and GTP levels, respectively.
source: Concurrently, there were +3% and +9% shifts in ppGpp and GTP levels, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The UGA ΔmlaF strain maintained consistent levels of GTP relative to WT, with a −3% decrease in ppGpp and a +3% increase in pppGpp.
source: In contrast, the UGA ΔmlaF strain maintained consistent levels of GTP relative to WT, with a −3% decrease in ppGpp and a +3% increase in pppGpp (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In every ΔmlaC or ΔmlaF generated in the UW WT background, the obgE* SNP repaired itself.
source: Indeed, sanger sequencing revealed that in every ΔmlaC or ΔmlaF we generated, the obgE* SNP repaired itself: a phenomenon we observed 15/15 times (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The ΔmlaC, obgE::kan, pMMB67EH-obgE* strains accumulated unique mutations with unknown implications.
source: Unfortunately, the ΔmlaC, obgE::kan, pMMB67EH-obgE* strains accumulated unique mutations with unknown implications that prevent legitimate phenotypic comparisons (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 3.

claim: ObgE is implicated in various physiological processes rooted in the regulation and homeostasis of the stringent response alarmone (p)ppGpp.
source: ObgE is implicated in various physiological processes rooted in the regulation and homeostasis of the stringent response alarmone (p)ppGpp (Persky et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Persky et al., 2009).

claim: ppGpp inhibits de novo fatty acid biosynthesis and by proxy GPL biosynthesis.
source: Additional evidence shows ppGpp inhibits de novo fatty acid biosynthesis and by proxy GPL biosynthesis (Heath et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Heath et al., 1994).

claim: Mla-null mutants have compromised OM asymmetry.
source: The first is that Mla-null mutants have compromised OM asymmetry (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).

claim: Mla-null mutants exhibit increased OM vesiculation.
source: The second is that Mla-null mutants exhibit increased OM vesiculation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PldA-derived fatty acids stimulate de novo lipid A biosynthesis in E. coli.
source: Lastly, there is strong genetic evidence in E. coli that PldA-derived fatty acids stimulate de novo lipid A biosynthesis (May and Silhavy, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (May and Silhavy, 2018).

claim: Only the UW ΔmlaF strain was hypersusceptible to serine hydroxamate treatment with a 50% reduction in growth.
source: When we treated with serine hydroxamate, which induces stringent response, only the UW ΔmlaF strain was hypersusceptible with a 50% reduction in growth (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: No other Δmla strain tested exhibited a phenotype to serine hydroxamate treatment.
source: No other Δmla strain tested exhibited a phenotype (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Only the UW ΔmlaF strain was hypersusceptible to cerulenin treatment.
source: Similarly, when we treated with cerulenin, which inhibits fatty acid biosynthesis, only the UW ΔmlaF strain was hypersusceptible (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ΔmlaC deletions made in the UW WT (mlaC::kan MJP1 and MJP2) which had repaired the obgE* allele, looked identical to WT for both serine hydroxamate and cerulenin treatments.
source: In both cases, ΔmlaC deletions made in the UW WT (mlaC::kan MJP1 and MJP2) which had repaired the obgE* allele, looked identical to WT for both treatments (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: De novo GPL levels were significantly reduced upon induction of stringent response with serine hydroxamate across all strains.
source: Across the board, de novo GPL levels were significantly reduced upon induction of stringent response with serine hydroxamate, confirming that elevated ppGpp levels indirectly inhibit GPL biosynthesis (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: A. baumannii mla mutants exhibit no defects in anterograde transport.
source: Here, we show conclusively that A. baumannii mla mutants exhibit no defects in anterograde transport.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the OMV pulse-chase assay.

claim: An allele of the GTPase obgE is synthetically sick in the absence of Mla.
source: Furthermore, we identify an allele of the GTPase obgE that is synthetically sick in the absence of Mla; providing another link between cell envelope homeostasis and stringent response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing genetic interactions and phenotypic effects.

claim: The UW ΔmlaF strain decreased expression of fadE.
source: We further found that the UW ΔmlaF mutant decreased expression of fadE, the priming step in β-oxidation (Campbell and Cronan, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA-seq and a citation to published literature (Campbell and Cronan, 2002).

claim: ObgE and SpoT co-purify in a potentially physiologically relevant manner.
source: There is additional evidence suggesting that ObgE and SpoT co-purify in a potentially physiologically relevant manner (Wout et al., 2004) and that ObgE plays a role in stringent response nucleotide homeostasis (Persky et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Wout et al., 2004; Persky et al., 2009).

claim: ObgE plays a role in stringent response nucleotide homeostasis.
source: There is additional evidence suggesting that ObgE and SpoT co-purify in a potentially physiologically relevant manner (Wout et al., 2004) and that ObgE plays a role in stringent response nucleotide homeostasis (Persky et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Persky et al., 2009).

claim: The allele of obgE in the UW strain plays an aberrant role in the stringent response, which is further exacerbated in the absence of a functional Mla system.
